grid.title: What the data says about {hero}
grid.intro: Measured results from public match data. Each shows only when it passes its rule; open “Why?” for the numbers behind it.{strong, select, yes { They show where the wins come from, not why the hero is designed that way.} other {}}
grid.empty: No result clears its sample and confidence rules in this scope yet. Try a longer window or a broader rank band.

metric.wonLow: {rate} of {count} matches won (Low sample, not compared)

shift.statement: {subject}’s win rate {direction, select, rising {increased} other {decreased}} {points} percentage points, from {previous} in the 7 days before to {current} in the last 7 days.
shift.rule: Both windows have at least 200 matches, their 95% intervals don’t overlap, and the change is at least 1 percentage point.

patch.title: Recent shift
patch.statement: {subject}’s win rate was {points} percentage points {direction, select, rising {higher} other {lower}} in the days after the “{patch}” update ({after}) than in the 7 days before ({before}).
patch.rule: Both periods have at least 200 matches, their 95% intervals don’t overlap, and the change is at least 1 percentage point.
patch.caveat: This shows timing only. Other changes in the same days (player mix, other heroes) can move a win rate too.

pairing.matchupStatement: Shows a {positive, select, yes {positive} other {negative}} matchup against {other}{relation, select, lane { in lane} other {}} in the selected dataset: {rate} won over {count} {relation, select, lane {lane matchups} other {matches}}.
pairing.synergyStatement: {subject} won {rate} of {count} matches with {other} on the same team in the selected dataset.
pairing.result: {rate} won over {count} {relation, select, lane {lane matchups} other {matches}}
pairing.rule: At least 200 {relation, select, lane {lane matchups} other {matches}}, a 95% interval entirely {positive, select, yes {above} other {below}} 50%, and a gap of at least 1 percentage point.

popularBuild.title: Most-selected build
popularBuild.statement: “{build}” was selected at game start in {count} {subject} matches, {share} of matches using a tracked build.
popularBuild.rule: The tracked build selected in the most matches, with at least 200 of them.
popularBuild.caveat: Tracked builds are the most-favorited published builds; matches using other builds aren’t counted.

highBuild.title: High-performing build
highBuild.statement: Matches where “{build}” was selected were won {rate} of the time, above {subject}’s {heroRate} overall.
highBuild.rule: At least 200 matches, and the build’s 95% interval sits entirely above the hero’s win rate by at least 1 percentage point.
highBuild.caveat: Players choose their build, so this compares groups of matches; it doesn’t isolate the build’s effect.

itemTrend.statement: {item} was bought in {current} of {subject} matches in the last 7 days, {direction, select, up {up} other {down}} from {previous} in the 7 days before.
itemTrend.rule: Both windows have at least 200 hero matches and 200 buyers, the buy-rate 95% intervals don’t overlap, and the change is at least 3 percentage points.

split.statement: {subject}’s win rate is highest in {best} ({bestRate}) and lowest in {worst} ({worstRate}).
split.rule: {by, select, rank {Rank bands} other {Match-length groups}} with at least 200 matches; the highest group’s 95% interval sits entirely above the lowest group’s.
split.rankCaveat: Only matches with an average rank are counted.

rankPopularity.title: Pick rate by rank
rankPopularity.statement: Frequently picked by {band} players: in {pick} of {band} matches, vs {overall} across all ranks.
rankPopularity.rule: At least 200 matches in the band, a pick rate at least 1.5× the all-rank rate, and non-overlapping 95% intervals. Match counts are estimated as hero picks ÷ 12.
rankPopularity.caveat: {subject} is popular there; popularity alone says nothing about results.

purchaseTiming.title: Purchase timing
purchaseTiming.statement: {item} bought at {range} has a {rate} win rate: {gap}pp higher than the next purchase phase, and {adjusted}pp higher after the net-worth adjustment.
purchaseTiming.rule: A phase is named only when it has 200+ purchases, its 95% interval sits entirely above every other phase’s, it leads the next phase by at least 1 point, and it also leads by at least 1 point after the net-worth adjustment.
purchaseTiming.caveat: Observational: players who buy at different times are in different games (lead, net worth, match length). The adjustment re-weights for net worth only; this is not a causal estimate.
